News.title: Brit woman, 21, charged with murder after ‘stabbing partner, 33, to death with zombie knife’ at their luxury Thai villa
News.content:
MURDER PROBE Brit woman, 21, charged with murder after ‘stabbing partner, 33, to death with zombie knife’ at their luxury Thai villa

A BRITISH woman who allegedly stabbed her boyfriend to death with a 20-inch hunting knife at their luxury Thai villa has been pictured.

Isabelle Violet Carreras, 20, has been charged with murder after her partner, a 33-year-old Brit businessman, was found dead in Pattaya.





The victim was found in the shower with stab wounds to his back, torso and left hand, as well as a pillow under his head.

One of the victim’s concerned friends had previously alerted police because the businessman was not picking up his phone.

The worried pal rushed over to his mate’s luxury home in Pattaya where he found the body in the bathroom.

The suspect Carreras, originally from Stafford, was lying next to him sobbing.



Inside the villa, cops described seeing blood-stained furniture as well as several items being thrown across the ground.

Officers also found blood on tiles and cabinets in the bathroom and several towels dyed red from the blood of the Brit.



They allege his wife was trying to clean up the crime scene before they rushed round to the villa.

Initial investigations point towards the body being killed at least six hours before it was found.

Police said that a 20-inch zombie-knife found in the sink was the murder weapon and that it had showed signs of being wiped clean.

The wife was questioned at the scene as cops reportedly found cuts on her fingers.

She professed her innocence and claimed he had taken his own life.



After claiming the Brit’s death was a suicide, Carreras then alleged he was “really into grass recently”, referring to Marijuana, and that he “had been taking six strips of Valium daily”.

Police Colonel Nattapon Phongsuksakul said they were combing through CCTV footage at their home to determine how the fatal stabbing unfolded.

He said: “It is a murder case inside a house, with the body ultimately being found in the bathroom.

“The wife denied committing the murder. However, based on the wounds, it is difficult for us to accept that claim because there was clearly a stab wound to the back.”

Thai police have confirmed that they are treating this as a murder case, not an act of self-defence.



Neighbours have recalled the couple moving into their house two weeks earlier.

They said the pair were known to smoke cannabis regularly with Phongsuksakul confirming tests are being ran to determine if it had been used prior to the Brit’s death.

Phongsuksakul also said: “Based on the evidence gathered so far, investigators believe Ms Isabelle Violet Carreras was responsible for the killing.

“She has now been formally charged with murder, but she continues to deny the allegation during questioning.

“The investigation is still ongoing. We are still awaiting the full autopsy report, forensic examination results and DNA analysis before finalising the case file.”



He added: “There is evidence that cannabis was consumed, and we believe it is possible that cannabis intoxication contributed to the suspect‘s actions.”

Police alleged the murder took place at 4am local time but that no one was notified until 9.30am.

The couple was initially believed to have been married, but police have not confirmed this yet.

The Foreign Office told The Sun: “We are supporting the families of two British nationals in Thailand and are in contact with the local authorities.”

News.title: Shocking moment idiot sets off firework directly into packed pub during annual celebrations in Australia
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a firework was set off directly into a packed pub during annual celebrations, sending revellers ducking for cover as the rocket exploded among the crowd.

Footage shows a man holding a large firework at a horizontal angle before firing it straight towards a busy venue in Australia.





The explosive then detonates in the direction of people enjoying the night’s festivities.

A clip shows the firework launching towards an Irish pub before erupting into a fireball as people inside and outside scramble for safety.

The pair then run from the scene as shocked locals are seen diving for cover amid the blast.

It is not yet known if anyone inside the pub, named Shenannigans, was injured, and no arrests have been confirmed.



The incident took place in the Northern Territory, Australia, during the annual Territory Day celebrations.

Territory Day is the only day of the year when fireworks can be legally bought and set off without a permit, and has built a reputation for chaotic and high-risk scenes.

It marks the anniversary of the Northern Territory gaining self-government.

Fire crews were called out to multiple blazes, with grass fires, building damage and at least one vehicle fire reported during the celebrations.



Authorities said 36 people were injured during the night, down from 41 the previous year.

Further footage showed fireworks being fired from vehicles and roads, including from the back of a ute using handheld devices, with rockets seen shooting across public areas.

One resident said a family repeatedly set off fireworks close to their vehicle before it eventually caught fire.



She said: “There was a family with a lot of fireworks, they had a Kia Carnival and had the tailgate up… as they went on through the night they were setting off fireworks closer and closer to the car, and the inevitable happened.”

She added: “They were shooting out in all the directions, when the firies arrived they had to back off in the beginning because they were actually getting fireworks at them.”

Despite the chaos, Northern Territory Police said the majority of people celebrated safely and responsibly, stressing the dangerous behaviour seen online was not typical.

A police spokesperson said: “The behaviour shown in this footage is reckless and does not reflect how most Territorians celebrated the day.”

“While incidents like this attract attention, they are the exception, not the rule.



“We urge anyone considering this type of dangerous behaviour to think twice. It puts people at risk and can have serious consequences.”

Officers also confirmed it is now illegal to possess fireworks after the permitted period ends.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A government warning has since urged residents to hand in leftover fireworks, warning they become unstable over time and can pose serious risks if stored.

Emergency services remained on high alert throughout the night, with officials praising crews for dealing with multiple fires and incidents across the celebrations.

News.title: Our picture postcard village of 700 residents has been earmarked for 1,200 asylum seekers…there’s been ‘no consultation’
News.content:
BORDER RIFT Our picture postcard village of 700 residents has been earmarked for 1,200 asylum seekers…there’s been ‘no consultation’

RESIDENTS are stunned their picture postcard Yorkshire village has been earmarked for accommodating 1,200 asylum seekers – four years after a nearly identical plan by the Tories was scrapped.

The bombshell announcement late last month allegedly came without anyone being consulted in the Domesday Book village of Linton-on-Ouse, near York, in North Yorkshire.





The aim is to use the former air base, RAF Linton-on-Ouse, which has been in the village since 1937, to house migrants after flying operations ceased in 2019.

It was recently announced that the site would be one of three former military bases, to be turned into migrant housing as part of Labour’s plans to close asylum hotels.

The other two sites include a Ministry of Defence facility in Bicester, Oxfordshire and RAF Barnham in Suffolk.

Meanwhile, on Friday, the Home Office U-turned on further plans for 83 asylum seekers dubbed “Migrant Street” in Stoke Heath, Shropshire.

When the plan was first mooted for Linton four years ago, there was massive opposition.

Previous plans to use the base as an asylum centre for up to 1,500 single men were abandoned in 2022 amid fierce protests from local residents and the threat of legal action from the former Hambleton District Council.

Now, residents say the arguments are the same as four years ago – there is nothing for a further 1,200 men to do in the village.

Their only shop had been shut and boarded up for four years; there is only one pub in the village and just a few buses to York every day.



Many were also quick to point out that outgoing PM Keir Starmer himself had rubbished the idea when it was a Tory initiative.

There are also concerns that the base will cost millions to be made fit for purpose, and the village will be targeted by right wing activists who will turn the village into a “another Southampton”.

Jackie Holder, 77, said: “I think it is going to go through this time. That is my gut feeling.



“They managed to stop it last time. It will be the same again with the protests in the village. I hope I am wrong.

“If it was 12 to 15 hundred families, I would say ‘come’.

“We have a lovely village school which has been much depleted with the RAF base closed because there was a lot of RAF kids.



“But 1,200 men? We are only seven hundred of us in this village…”

Trevor Dawson, 76, moved back to the village, where his family has lived for generations, including a granddad who was the local blacksmith, in 1992.

He said: “There are new houses on the land running down to the camp and how they going to sell now?

“They live in a bubble in Westminster. We are on the fringes, out of sight and out of mind. I heard about the announcement on local TV.

“There was no consultation again. Some blokes from the Home Office said we have got to put them somewhere because we are closing all the hotels down.”



Della Blood, 62, heard about the plans on the morning news and described them as “absolutely ridiculous”.

She said: “I know it was thrown out four years ago but think it has got in the right door this time.

“I don’t think the protesters will succeed this time. Why don’t they open one of the private schools which has shut down?



“I think it is utterly, utterly bonkers. We don’t want 1,200 men roaming the streets…

“We have got our house for sale and won’t be selling that now. I kept my head really below the parapet last time. But I was stunned when I saw the announcement.”

Grenville Long, 66, described the plans as “totally inappropriate” and said migrants come to the UK because the country has become a “honeypot”.



The Sun reported last month how migrants will be forced to pay back the cost of their accommodation in a student loan-style scheme and will be stopped from getting settled status if they do.

But the backlash against the announcement for Linton shows little sign of abating.

Prof Olga Matthias, who is leading the new campaign to fight the plans, said: “I only heard about the announcement because I got a telephone call from a journalist asking me what I thought about it.

“I said ‘Excuse me?’ What is needed is not knee-jerk comments but a policy with some substance behind it.

“The Government needs a clearly thought through long term policy – preferably with cross party support.”



Walking her dog, Annie said: “It is an absolutely crazy idea. They are just taking them out of one area and putting them in a rural one, where they will be forgotten about.

“Keir Starmer was against it because the Conservatives proposed it. Now he is proposing to do exactly the same thing. You can’t win.”

Peter Starkey, 77, said: “I am sure there will be a fight. It is gong to be tragic but what can we do but oppose this?”

A man, who asked not be named, said the announcement coincided with the buyers of their house pulling out. “The house is worthless now. I never dreamed this could happen,” he claimed.

“They will be free to roam around the village outnumbering us.



“Keir Starmer was dead against it when the Conservatives tried it so why does he think it is a good idea now?”

Helen Kirby, 74, a former organiser against the scheme four years ago, said: “It is an incredible shock.

“The Government we have now criticised the previous Government for the same actions, Keir Starmer in particular.



“It is totally inappropriate. The company which owns the former military housing on the base has beautifully renovated them for rent and I am sure people are already backing out.

“The community spirit in the village is tremendous. We have always had a very transient community because of the RAF base and have embraced that.

“We have a lot of ex RAF men who live in the village because they wanted to stay here.

“They want to live here although I am not so sure about that now. That I find is a real sadness. Our family have been since 1885 in this property. We have worked hard with the community to build a fantastic community spirit.

“Now we have people who want to run a mile but cannot sell their property. The Home Officer are arrogant and condescending. The last four years have not changed anything.



“We don’t stand a chance because the Government is saying it is going to make sure Linton has asylum seekers sent to it.

“I should be enjoying retirement. We were until that absolutely cruel statement.

“We will do everything we can but I think a lot of people are still in shock and very angry…

“We are a quiet, just get on with it, village. They wanted to build houses on the former airfield but they will not want to do that now.”

Andre Chaplin, 57, who worked on the RAF base as a civilian for 25 years before being made redundant, said: “It is awful.



“I have lived here 36 years and it is a real community. You need anything you just knock on a neighbour’s door.

“We will fight it. We have Yorkshire grit…

“My friend rang me up because she had heard the announcement on TV. I rang my brother who lives in Australia and could not believe it.”

Pensioner Helen Jones, who has lived in the village 20 years, said: “Four years ago, we said ‘no we would not have it’. But the RAF camp has continued to be empty.

“We have got one shop. The bus only goes to York. So, it is a bit of a worry. We knew anything about it until the time it was announced, which is awful really.”



The leader of North Yorkshire Council, Cllr Carl Les, said in a statement: “It’s important to be clear from the outset that we do not object to the government’s desire to house asylum seekers with dignity in safe and secure accommodation.

“However, we agree with many of the points made, and the concerns expressed by residents in the hundreds of correspondences we have received already, and we do not believe that Linton–on–Ouse is an appropriate location to house potentially 1,200 single adult males.

“We share the views of many leading voices in our region that this plan by the Home Office is flawed, that the site is completely inappropriate and that it was found to be so following a thorough investigation only a few years ago.

“The deterioration of the site only makes the issues raised at that time more relevant.”

He continued to say that the council was “seriously disappointed” that a media announcement was made by the Home Office before the council was notified.



Cllr Les added officials have told the council that “no decision has yet been made” with a final decision expected by the end of this year.

He said in summary: “In short, this is the wrong proposal in the wrong location evidenced by the fact the site has been considered and rejected previously on the basis that it is not suitable.”

Border Security and Asylum Minister Alex Norris said: “We promised to close every asylum hotel and hand them back to communities, and that is exactly what we are doing.

“Twenty more hotels have closed, and hotel numbers have more than halved since their peak.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Instead, we’re moving asylum seekers into ex-military sites that are a far cry from the hotels the last Government left us with.



“This is a system being brought back under control – and we will not stop until the job is done.”

News.title: Pakistani grooming gang leader deemed ‘unsafe’ and ‘high risk’ to children before release from prison
News.content:
RAPIST FREED Pakistani grooming gang leader deemed ‘unsafe’ and ‘high risk’ to children before release from prison

THE ringleader of the Rochdale grooming gang was deemed “unsafe” to be released and “high risk” to children before he was freed from prison.

Shabir Ahmed, 73, walked out of HMP Leeds on licence but will not be deported to Pakistan due to a 55-year-old law.





He served just 14 years of a 22-year sentence after he was convicted of 30 child rapes in 2012.

Ahmed was released from prison on Thursday and is staying in a bail hostel where he is banned from Rochdale and Oldham.

Now, documents reveal Ahmed was rejected for parole in October 2024 because of his risk of reoffending and refusal to engage with rehabilitation programmes, reports The Telegraph.

It was the third time Ahmed’s release was refused after his refusal to accept guilt and displaying “risk factors” – including believing it was “acceptable to abuse a child”.

Ahmed was also deemed to pose a “very high risk of serious harm” towards children three years ago, The Guardian reports.

The paedophile also attempted to seriously injure another prisoner.

But the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) released the ringleader after 14 years as his 22-year sentence had an automatic release date two-thirds of the way through.

Victims of the paedophile ring were also promised Ahmed would be deported after he was released from prison.



However, due to a loophole in the Immigration Act 1971, Ahmed is set to stay in the country despite having his British citizenship removed.

One survivor of the grooming gang, using the alias Ruby, told the BBC: “We were told they would all be deported once released, but not one of them has been deported.

“We need these laws to be updated. Laws need to change, and victims need to be heard.

“I was 12 years old when this started and still getting failed.

“There are broken victims because of a broken system. I am scared for my safety and my children’s safety.”



“Amber”, not her real name, was raped and sexually exploited by Shabir Ahmed.

She said in a statement: “I am absolutely furious that no one contacted me to tell me that Shabir Ahmed was going to be released – not the Prison Service, not Victim Liaison, no one.

“I had to find out about it from the media, in the week of his release.

“For the past three nights I haven’t been able to sleep. I’ve been physically sick over this. I’ve had to ring my children’s school because I’m scared for their safety.

“He has contacts in Rochdale. They operated as a gang – so even if he stays out of Rochdale, he could still get other men to do what he wants.



“I feel like I’ve been let down all over again. Greater Manchester Police accepted I was a victim and that I should have been protected, but there is still zero victim support.”

After facing mounting calls for Ahmed’s deportation, the government is said to be considering imposing tough visa sanctions or withholding foreign aid to force Pakistan to take back Ahmed.

Ahmed has been stripped of his British citizenship but cannot be deported due to the 1971 Immigration Act that forbids the removal of a small group of Commonwealth citizens who arrived in the UK more than 50 years ago.

The divorced dad-of-four, who forced his victims to call him “Daddy”, arrived in the UK before 1973.

Home Secretary, Shabana Mahmood, is planning to scrap the legal loophole stopping Ahmed from being deported.



PM in waiting Andy Burnham has backed victims’ calls to remove the “vile criminal” from the country.

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch also weighed in on the case, calling for Ahmed’s removal she said: “It’s absolutely disgusting that this man has been let out.

“He should be deported, and we’re going to do everything within our power to make sure that he is, but we’re going to need the Government to get behind us.

“Whether it’s Keir Starmer or Andy Burnham, what I want to see is them agreeing with us, so that we can get that amendment through.”

Sir Keir Starmer’s spokesperson said: “It is fair to say the PM would always want to see these vile criminals deported.”



They added however: “We cannot deport someone who is protected by the 1971 Immigration Act, these are the same provisions which have protected many individuals caught up in the Windrush crisis.”

The leader of the paedophile gang was jailed for 22 years in 2012 after being convicted of two counts of rape, one sex assault, trafficking and conspiracy to engage in sexual activity with a child.

He plied girls as young as 13 with drink and drugs before abusing them with eight of his friends.

During his trial, he exposed his naked torso in the dock and threw a clump of chest hair on the floor, saying of one victim: “She would have seen this.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Following his release, he will now be housed in a bail hostel in the north of England, costing the taxpayer an estimated £120 a night.



The MoJ and probation service will spend thousands of pounds on implementing restrictions on him after his release.

News.title: Perv who pretended to be a caretaker to sexually assault kids at lido is caught decades later after DNA breakthrough
News.content:
SICK ATTACK Perv who pretended to be a caretaker to sexually assault kids at lido is caught decades later after DNA breakthrough

A SERIAL sex offender who disguised as a caretaker to abuse kids has FINALLY been caught decades later thanks to a DNA breakthrough.

David Pearce has been sentenced to 18 years in prison after pleading guilty to seven sex offences.





In 1990 Pearce impersonated a caretaker to lure four young kids into a lido in east London.

After claiming he was searching for some lost keys, he cornered the children into a changing area before forcing them to strip off and assaulting them.

The youngest victim was aged just eight years old.

The kids immediately ran to a local police station to report the crime, allowing officials to collect DNA samples which unfortunately at the time did not match anyone on the database.

Another incident in 1996 followed a similar pattern of a 13-year-old girl being forced into some shrubbery under the false pretence of searching for keys.

She too was assaulted in the Barking park.



After officers exhausted all lines of enquiry, the cases were filed pending further investigative opportunities coming to light.

For years his disturbing crimes went unsolved, until a recent DNA breakthrough changed everything.

In 2019 Pearce was arrested for an unrelated offence of voyeurism, where he had to provide DNA samples.

The DNA he provided was a one in a billion match to the suspect at the lido.

Detectives decided to dig a bit deeper and review similar historical reports, including the one in 1996.



It was at this point that the park victim confirmed Pearce as the assailant in an identification parade.

Police had also discovered Pearce to be living in the area around that time.

With all of the evidence piling against the Cambridgeshire man, police were able to finally charge him for his horrific crimes.

Detective Constable Tony Anionwu from the Met’s Specialist Crime Unit said: “Pearce was a predator who disguised himself as someone in a position of trust to exploit and assault young children.

“His actions had a lasting impact, and I would like to thank the victim-survivors for their unwavering resilience and profound patience while we strived for justice.



“As a force we remain committed to securing justice for anyone who has experienced a sexual assault, no matter when they occurred, and over the past five years we have more than tripled arrests and charges for this crime.”

On Wednesday May 6 Pearce denied a further four counts of indecent assault, six counts of attempting an act of indecency with a child and two counts of indecency with a child – all in the 1990s.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The prosecution chose to leave those charges on file after his guilty pleas were entered.

On Friday June 3, Pearce was sentenced to 18 years in prison at Snaresbrook Crown Court.

News.title: Girl, 7, left ‘fighting for her life’ after being mauled by pack of SIX dogs that ripped off her scalp in brutal attack
News.content:
SAVAGE ATTACK Girl, 7, left ‘fighting for her life’ after being mauled by pack of SIX dogs that ripped off her scalp in brutal attack

A GIRL was left fighting for her life after being scalped and savaged by a pack of six stray dogs in a brutal daylight attack.

Patricia Edmiston, 7, was violently ambushed by a pack of dogs that savagely ripped off her scalp and tore into her legs while she was playing outside in California.





She was rushed to hospital in a critical condition and is now battling for survival.

The attack unfolded in Corning, around 170 miles northwest of San Francisco, where Patricia Edmiston was near Barham Avenue and Bosque Avenue at around 12.30pm on Saturday.

The animals were later seized by Tehama County authorities and taken to the local animal shelter as the investigation continues.

Police have not confirmed the breed of the dogs and their current status remains unclear.

Though officials had not released the child’s identity, her grandmother Monica Edmiston named her publicly as Patricia, describing the severity of the injuries.

Monica said the dogs ripped Patricia’s scalp off and that the little girl was “fighting for her life” in hospital with injuries across her body.

It is still not known how Patricia came into contact with the pack or what she was doing moments before the attack.

The grandmother said Patricia was airlifted to UC Davis Medical Center, about 100 miles from the scene, where she underwent emergency surgery and remains in critical condition.



She added that the child’s father and brothers have stayed by her side every day, but the family is struggling under huge strain.

“They are sleeping in their car in Sacramento just to stay close to Patricia, and they need help to cover basic necessities like gas and food,” she wrote on GoFundMe.

Around $4,100 (£30,697) has been raised so far, with donations now paused after passing the initial target.



Deputies have spoken to witnesses and examined the scene, but no arrests or charges have been made nearly a week on from the attack.

The Corning Union Elementary School District also confirmed the incident on Facebook and said Patricia was being treated at UC Davis.

Her grandmother said the child’s strength has been remarkable, calling her resilience “inspiring everyone around her.”

She shared a photo of Patricia in hospital, heavily bandaged on her head and hand, with a Hello Kitty toy beside her as she managed a small smile with family.

Other family photos showed the girl smiling and playing happily before the attack, including images of her with siblings and a lost tooth grin.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Monica said Patricia was originally due to be discharged from hospital on Thursday.

She added: “Patricia and her family would like to thank everyone for their prayers, thoughts, and donations. The love the town of Corning showed was overwhelming.”

News.title: Tupac murder case could be THROWN OUT just weeks before bombshell trial over icon’s killing after cops ‘lose key files’
News.content:
COPS have lost potentially key files in the Tupac Shakur murder probe which could impact the upcoming trial into the rap icon’s murder.

A vast array of reports and evidence gathering surrounding the gangland hit on Shakur, held by Las Vegas cops, have been lost or gone missing, The Sun can reveal.





LAPD officers’ reports examining the 1996 assassination of Tupac in Las Vegas have been not been located by prosecutors during their three-year case preparation.

Two computer floppy discs and a micro cassette featuring years of information from Vegas homicide detectives have also been deemed unusable.

And a long term Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) probe into accused murder suspect Duane “Keefe D” Davis’s alleged gang and criminal enterprises has not been made available.

That project, which ran for at least a decade, included surveillance, meets with informants and information gathering on Davis’ entire alleged criminal enterprise – which he boasted in his book was worth billions from his drug dealing.

The staggering twist emerged this week – just five weeks before Davis’s trial for murder is set to begin on August 10.

One family friend of Keefe claimed he is “delighted at the news, because he was uncertain about what intel they had on him over 15 years of being on his a**”.

Veteran Vegas prosecutor and Chief Deputy District Attorney Marc DiGiacomo confirmed the revelation.

DiGiacomo told a court hearing in Clark County how he had gathered details of the original investigations by LA and Vegas cops, including liaising with original Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department’s lead detective, Brent Becker.



Other information was gathered from a 2004/5 LAPD task force examining Biggie Smalls’s murder, which had taken place in March 1997.

Another huge file featuring “tens of thousands of pages” came from LAPD detectives Greg Kading and Daryn Dupree. They were tasked with probing the murders of Tupac and the Notorious B.I.G in the late 2000s.

But DiGiacomo admitted that Becker told him files he recalled were in his original investigation in the wake of the September 7 1996 shooting – were missing from the evidence.



DiGiacomo said: “We located Detective Becker because there was a lot of information in the Biggie Smalls murder about communications between Metro and LAPD, related to the Biggie Smalls investigation. When I talked to Becker, I sent him the number of reports we have from him.

“And he indicated that there were substantially more reports than that.”

Becker explained that several files were stored on old computer discs – known as floppy discs – in a bid to stop information leaking to the media about Pac’s death.



DiGiacomo said: “They began to save their reports that they wrote, to two, 3.5 inch, floppy discs.

“We searched Metro and determined that in 2018, Detective Mogg sent two 3.5 floppy discs, and DVDs that appears to be surveillance that they, years and years and years ago, had of Mr Davis in California, two small cassettes, and then there was a micro cassette that was sent over.

“One disc, they found no information on. The other disc was corrupted.

“So we have no additional report from Detective Becker. The two videos, as well as two audios were able to be downloaded, the micro-cassette was not able to be.“

There was also confusion about whether other notes from both LAPD task force probes have survived.



DiGiacomo noted: “What we do not have is an entire copy of what else the Task Force did, as it relates to their investigation of Biggie Smalls and or Tupac. That’s just not in our possession.”

It’s understood files may not be released by agencies over fears details of informants and “snitches” may feature, putting their lives in danger.

In the 1990s, Davis, by his own admission in taped conversations with law enforcement and his book Compton Street Legend, was one of the biggest distributors of narcotics across the USA. Davis’s attorney has since claimed the book was fictionalised.



Davis had claimed he had direct connections to Mexican and Colombian cartels allowing him to bring in shipments of 350 kilos of cocaine regularly.

His activities led DEA agents to launch a full scale probe into his gang and nationwide connections.

Davis himself admitted that “snitches” were talking to the “Feds” about his criminal enterprises and even “on the ground everyone in Compton talked about how he and other Crips killed Tupac.”

However, that vast file of information has not been provided to the Clark County District Attorney’s office.

DiGiacomo said: “The only people who may have additional information are the DEA. And we don’t have the ability to subpoena the DEA for those records.”



The prosecutor made his admissions to judge Carli Kierny as he revealed the evidence he has shared with Davis’ defence lawyer Mike Sanft during a court hearing into the case last month.

Speaking to The Sun, Sanft said: “The Clark County District Attorney has had 30 years to put their case together.

“They re-tested ‘evidence’ to a grand jury in 2023 that led to Mr Davis being arrested in his home.

“The State ought to avoid this embarrassment of a case and dismiss it before we have to put on a trial.”

Davis, who boasted to being The Godfather Of Compton, faces life in prison if found guilty.



In his memoir, he wrote how the “Feds”, LAPD and FBI were spying on him after Pac’s killing, alleging they had informants in his circles.

Why it’s taken so long for justice in the Tupac Shakur case By The Sun’s Senior Reporter Emma Parry, who has been reporting on the Tupac murder for over 10 years TUPAC fans have been waiting for justice for the iconic rapper for almost 30 years. Finally in September 2023 there appeared to be progress with the arrest of Duane “Keefe D” Davis – a former Southside Crip gangster from Compton, LA – who had been telling the world for years that he and his fellow “gang soldiers” were responsible for the hit. I’ve been reporting on the case for several years and it always appeared pretty cut and dry…Keefe had spent the past decade gaining notoriety by boasting about his alleged involvement in the shooting – now he was finally getting what he deserves. But despite Keefe running his mouth for years, I now believe a guilty verdict in August’s trial is far from guaranteed. Keefe describes in great detail in his memoir Compton Street Legend what went down the night Pac was shot, extracts from which The U.S. Sun has published. He claimed that he was offered a million dollars by rapper Diddy to “handle” Tupac and Suge Knight and when he and his Crip gangsters came across the pair driving near the Strip in Las Vegas on September 7, 1996, Keefe alleged he passed the gun to his nephew Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson who took the shot. Keefe said if Pac had been on his side: “I would have blast”. Keefe repeated the claims multiple times over the years, on YouTube channels, documentaries, and even in taped confessions to police, when he believed he could not be prosecuted. In one confession to the LAPD, Keefe appeared completely remorseless telling detectives: “We didn’t give a f**k…The ambulance [for Tupac] was parked right here next to us. That s**t was as funny as a motherf**ker.” The Sun has been publishing stories about Keefe’s self confessed involvement in the crime since 2018. I sent many links to his confessions to Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department, asking them why this man had not been arrested yet. They would thank me for the info but say that they could not comment because the case was still active. From the outside, it looked like no action was being taken at all. We spoke to former detectives involved in the case and documentary makers who all felt utterly frustrated at the lack of progress in the case. We even published a plea from former LAPD detective Greg Kading, who had probed the murders, urging Las Vegas cops to arrest Keefe, back in 2020. For years, the case appeared to have been forgotten and ignored, to be left forever unsolved. But finally, in the summer of 2023, we got word from our sources that there had been a huge development in the case. A secret grand jury was due to be held on whether or not Keefe should be indicted. I was dubious at first but around the same time a house in Henderson, Nevada, linked to Keefe, was raided in July as part of the Tupac investigation. Things were heating up. Later that summer, behind closed doors, jurors listened to hours of testimony from former cops, detectives, and coroners involved in the Tupac case and gangsters and associates of Keefe’s and Pac’s from back in the day. They were shown graphic photos of Tupac’s bullet-ridden body. After days of evidence, they decided there was enough evidence to prosecute Keefe. Once the secret documents were released I poured over the transcripts. While interesting, many of the witnesses were telling stories they’d heard second-hand. None of the prosecution witnesses had a clear look at who shot Pac. One witness Devonta Lee claimed another gangster called Big Dre took the shot – not Orlando. Maybe things weren’t as clear-cut as I first thought. Keefe was then arrested on September 30, 2023 at his home. Bodycam footage we obtained from the scene showed Keefe bragging to cops even as he was handcuffed in the back of a police car – telling officers he was involved in the “biggest case in Las Vegas history”. Following Keefe’s multiple appearances in court, he seems to have lost much of that bravado and now cuts a sad, lonely figure. Suffering from various health problems as a result of cancer, he’s struggling to cope with the brutalities of jail life and can’t get together enough money to afford his bail. He feels some of his old Southside Crip associates – men he handed wads of cash to in his glory days, have just abandoned him. Keefe is now desperate to get out of jail, and his defense stems is leaning on his claim that he completely made up his involvement in the Tupac murder for fame and money. He saw other people cashing in on the murder so he thought he would too. He reckons his confessions to police were all lies – he made it up because he was under a plea deal and thought it would help him beat his other charges. And, according to his previous lawyer Carl Arnold, he wasn’t even in Las Vegas on the night of the shooting. Arnold and Keefe’s new lawyer Mike Sanft are convinced he walk free and their secret weapon could be former Death Row Records boss Suge. As the only other person still alive from either car, Suge, currently in prison for a fatal hit and run, would be a key witness. Suge is the only person still alive who knows what went down – he saw the shooter. While he’s said he won’t testify at the trial, Suge has claimed in a TMZ interview from prison that Orlando was not the shooter, which again throws into doubt the accpeted version of events. Keefe and his lawyer are hoping they might be able to change his mind and persuade him to testify for the defence. And Suge holds the power to blow the prosecution’s case apart. And if Keefe walks free, will there ever be justice for Pac?

He recalled “a big meeting for our neighborhoods” with “all the homeys”.

He wrote: “I did all the talking and the Feds knew everything that I said to them because there were some informants”, which “caused the Feds to start following me round everywhere”.

Keefe claimed that an FBI agent had teams “on my a** from day one” and the DEA and other agencies spent 15 years building cases against him.



A friend of the one-time feared LA drug kingpin, who is currently awaiting trial in Clark County Detention Center, said: “Keefe is taking everything as a win the moment.

“He is in a positive frame of mind about the trial and believes the state cannot win. Some missing paperwork has not helped him.

“But the confirmation from the DA that so many law enforcement reports about his connections to Tupac will not be evidence makes him immensely happy.”

Davis has boasted to being the “shot caller” who oversaw a gang of South Side Compton Crips’ gunning down Tupac close to the Las Vegas strip in September 1996.

Not only did he confess in two taped police interviews, but also made similar claims in TV and online media appearances and in his memoir.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The trial is expected to start on August 10 and he has pleaded not guilty.

The Sun has reached out to Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Dept for comment.

News.title: Wimbledon star delivers own take on strict dress code as outfit catches the eye
News.content:
Wimbledon star delivers own take on strict dress code as outfit catches the eye

The Wimbledon tennis star has caused a commotion with her highly creative on-court clothing

View 2 Images Marta Kostyuk's dress has caused a commotion (Image: Getty)

Ukrainian tennis player Marta Kostyuk has captured attention at Wimbledon not only for her devastating skills with the racket but also for her eye-catching outfit. The 24-year-old's bridal-inspired tennis dress, which she first wore in 2024, has gone viral once more.

‌



Despite the All England Club's stringent dress code, Kostyuk's Wilson-designed ensemble has wowed fans and officials, rather than sparking controversy.

‌



The French Open semi-finalist is wearing a replica of her 2023 wedding gown, which was also created by Wilson. For this year's Wimbledon, Kostyuk has brought back the popular dress from two years ago, with it being dubbed the Marta Dress 2.0.

‌



It's crafted from a lace pattern that evokes a bride's veil and features a sheer white panel over her sleeveless dress. Wilson themselves have shared the dress on their social media, captioning it: "The grass dress code, reimagined by Marta."

The original Marta dress was available for £150 but has now sold out. It has attracted plenty of admirers on social media, too. Beneath a post of the dress on X, one fan said: "I love this. I should own this," while another added: " Like a wedding dress this is very, very beautiful".

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Tennis news: Novak Djokovic delivered bad news as star told to give up prize money READ MORE :

Under Wilson's post on Instagram, one person said: "So divine". A clearly impressed fan wrote: "Definitely the classiest, most beautiful, well-dressed on the Wimbledon court this year. Well done".

Wilson have stated that the design features "a sophisticated two-piece construction consisting of a bra, vest and skirt system, accented with technical lace detailing that elevates the look while maintaining the functionality required at the highest levels of the sport."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



They added: "What appears to be delicate, proves to be indestructible with a four-way stretch performance weave." Kostyuk clearly adores the dress.

She said: "To have a dress named after me, that was envisioned by me, feels absolutely surreal. Working with the Wilson team, especially Joelle, has been nothing short of amazing- I am able to help create looks that not only look beautiful, but are meant to perform on-court."

Any concern that the dress might prompt Wimbledon officials to intervene, given SW19's notorious dress code, was rapidly dismissed in 2024.

‌



Kostyuk's on-court kit is now in the possession of the Wimbledon Lawn Tennis Museum at the All England Club, owing to its enormous impact.

There is a remarkable nine-point dress code ruling for those competing at Wimbledon. The exhaustive guidelines essentially dictate that participants "must be dressed in suitable tennis attire that is almost entirely white."

View 2 Images Marta Kostyuk's dress has been a huge hit (Image: Getty)

‌



However, it is carefully noted that "White does not include off white or cream, while 'There should be no solid mass or panel of colouring.' It claims that 'logos formed by variations of material or patterns are not acceptable."

Kostyuk, who claimed the Madrid Open title earlier this year, had battled her way through to this stage at Wimbledon by defeating Nadia Podoroska in the first round and Anna Blinkova in the second.

Following her win against Podoroska, Kostyuk posted a picture of herself on court wearing the iconic dress, with the caption 'first dance complete'.

News.title: 'Andy Burnham facing immediate crises as PM - we must do the right thing'
News.content:
'Andy Burnham facing immediate crises as PM - we must do the right thing'

'International crises have a way of dragging our Prime Ministers out of the country altogether', the Chair of the Foreign Affairs Committee Dame Emily Thornberry writes

View 2 Images Andy Burnham has expressed hopes to be less in London (Image: Getty Images)

The next Prime Minister understandably wants to spend more time out of London, but international crises have a way of dragging our PMs out of the country altogether.

‌



Whether it’s Kiev or Qeshm Island, the inbox at No. 10 is going to be full of urgent meeting requests from the world over, and it’s going to need organising.

‌



First, the war in Europe. Ukraine’s long-range strikes on oil refineries are causing chaos in Moscow with petrol being rationed. Even Trump admits Zelenskyy is doing “pretty well”.

‌



Our landmark 100-year Partnership with Ukraine is more than military collaboration, it’s a friendship borne out of respect for their unimaginable bravery in the face of an illegal and barbaric invasion. We show up for Ukraine whenever they ask because the UK is a loyal friend and a serious player on the world stage. Russia, take note.

Russia planning attack on Poland to test NATO resolve, US claims READ MORE :

PM-in-waiting Andy Burnham rules out calling early general election READ MORE :

View 2 Images Emily Thornberry claimed international events force PMs to leave the country (Image: Thomas Krych/ZUMA Press Wire/REX/Shutterstock)

Next, there’s the European Union. The long-awaited second EU-UK Summit was supposed to be on 22 July but has been delayed. We need to get a new date in the diary as soon as possible, and we need to be really clear on what we want.

‌



Top of the list has to be an agreement on food standards, so our cheddar cheese can get to the continent and through the red tape before it becomes stilton! We also must link up our energy systems to make them more efficient and come to an agreement on taxing goods created at a high carbon cost. And we must make it easier for youngsters to travel in Europe.

We should point out once more that since the UK is playing a leading role in defending Europe, our defence industry should be in “SAFE” (which makes it easier for EU countries to buy our equipment). We also should push to make sure Ukraine is able to buy our stuff through the EU’s €90 billion Support Loan.

Organising the Middle East part of the inbox is easier said than done. The most urgent thing is what to do about Israel’s illegal E1 settlement. Netanyahu’s far-right government has reacted to our recognising Palestine by trying to build Israeli homes through the middle of it.

‌



There must be consequences. We should join the Netherlands, Ireland, Norway, Spain, Belgium, and many others to finally ban trade in goods and services with all settlements illegally built in Palestine.

The International Court of Justice has been clear that we should “abstain from entering into economic or trade dealings with Israel concerning Occupied Palestinian Territory”. The UK has been thinking about how we should respond to the judgement for over 700 days. Enough. Let’s do the right thing.

'In awe of how Lebanon keeps going'

I have returned from Lebanon with the Foreign Affairs Committee – a beautiful country full of contradictions.

‌



Walking along the Corniche in Beirut, with Israeli spy drones overhead, skyscrapers are being rebuilt even as the strikes continue.

Whilst the UK passionately debates how many refugees we can help, in Lebanon there are over 1m Syrians, as well as hundreds of thousands from Palestine. They have been there for years.

And now, with fighting in southern Lebanon, over 1m of the 5.5m-strong country have had to flee north. It was explained to me that, in the past few months, Lebanon has experienced the equivalent of 10m people moving from the north of England into the Home Counties. I am in awe of the way Lebanon is able to keep going.

‌



'Speaker could sing Wonderwall'

It’s not often you see parliamentarians united over anything, so I must say I was impressed to see Norwegian MPs doing the “Viking row” in their parliament to show support for their national team.

Ordinarily, Mr Speaker would not appreciate MPs doing something similar; according to Erskine May, we’re not allowed to sing.

But if we beat Mexico, you never know, he might lead us in a rousing rendition of Wonderwall.

Article continues below

'Fighting off the slug apocalypse'

Spare a thought for us city gardeners with our flower-pot gardens. Having survived the winter frost and a particularly wet spring, we spent early June fighting off the slug apocalypse, only to now find ourselves out watering our delphiniums twice a day.

And they said gardening was supposed to be relaxing!

News.title: UK drivers given new 34C heatwave alert as 'risk increases'
News.content:
UK drivers given new 34C heatwave alert as 'risk increases'

As the UK braces for another heatwave with temperatures set to soar to 34C, motorists are being urged to take extra care

View 3 Images Heat can make blowouts more likely (Image: SolStock via Getty Images)

As summer temperatures soar, drivers are being urged to stay alert, with the danger of tyre blowouts and vehicle-related problems rising during heatwaves.

‌



Another heatwave is poised to arrive in the UK, with temperatures again expected to reach 34C.

‌



James Harding, a tyre specialist at Blackcircles.com with more than 16 years of industry experience, said: "As temperatures rise, many drivers are unaware of how much strain summer conditions put on their vehicles. From tyre pressure fluctuations to overheating engines, small oversights can turn into major issues.

‌



"We're encouraging all motorists to take some precautions before setting off on any summer road trip to make sure their journeys are safe and stress-free."

How to prepare your vehicle for summer driving

Check tyre pressure regularly

Warm weather can impact tyre pressure, potentially diminishing grip, accelerating wear, and heightening the danger of a blowout if tyres are over- or under-inflated. As temperatures climb, the air within your tyres expands, raising pressure by approximately 0.1–0.2 bar for every 10°C.

View 3 Images Tyre condition is critical (Image: Yuto photographer via Getty Images)

‌



For the most precise reading, check tyre pressures when the tyres are cool, before driving or after the vehicle has been sitting in the shade, and always inflate them to the manufacturer's specified levels, as detailed in your owner's manual or on the fuel filler cap.

Top up fluids

Heat places additional pressure on your vehicle's engine, so it's important to routinely check oil and coolant levels, as insufficient fluid can result in overheating and mechanical failures. Motorists should also ensure their screen wash remains topped up to maintain clear visibility through bugs, dust, and pollen.

Shield yourself from sun glare

Sun glare is responsible for thousands of collisions annually, so clean your windscreen both inside and outside, replace worn wiper blades and keep a pair of sunglasses in your glovebox to enhance visibility.

‌



Monitor your dashboard

Summer conditions can push your vehicle's systems to their limits. If any warning lights illuminate on your dashboard, particularly temperature or engine alerts, pull over safely and investigate or seek assistance before any damage escalates. If you're unfamiliar with a warning light, be sure to look it up or contact a qualified mechanic.

View 3 Images Drivers have been alerted (Image: Rui Vieira/PA)

Check your air conditioning system

A working A/C is crucial not only for comfort but also for clearing windows, which can fog up in warm weather when humid air meets a cooler surface. Maintaining a complete field of vision is essential while driving. If your system isn't cooling properly, it may require re-gassing.

Article continues below

Prepare in advance for your journey

With more people venturing out on summer excursions, roads become increasingly congested, particularly around major motorways. To prevent lengthy delays and minimise the risk of stop-start traffic, which can cause engines to overheat and wear down brakes, check your route using traffic apps and aim to travel during quieter periods.

News.title: Intense eight-hour struggle for water in Malawi now a matter of life and death
News.content:
Intense eight-hour struggle for water in Malawi now a matter of life and death

Nada Farhoud travelled to Malawi, the fourth poorest country in the world, where almost 14 million people do not even have access to a decent toilet

View 9 Images Dina Nyati and Befa Kamoto walk back to their village after collecting water from a hand dug well (Image: WaterAid/ LeeAnn Olwage)

At 3am every morning, Dina Njati begins an exhausting eight-hour struggle to provide her family with water.

‌



The 37-year-old climbs down a steep hillside before filling a 20-litre container from a tiny muddy pond and hauling it back home on her head. Then she does it again until she has collected the water her family needs to cook, wash their clothes and bathe. But the gruelling trek is only part of her ordeal.

‌



The only water source serving her village of Mkambabisi, Malawi, is often so contaminated that it leaves both Dina and her young daughter sick. “It has happened so many times. We know it’s the water,” she said. “But we don’t say it out loud because where else are we going to get water?”

‌



Sadly, Dina’s struggle is far from unique. Across Malawi, one in three people lack access to clean water, while almost 14 million people - more than half the population - do not have a decent toilet.

View 9 Images Trinity and her one-year-old daughter Unity wash their hands outside the Kangolwa Health Centre (Image: WaterAid/ LeeAnn Olwage)

Millions of people across Southern Africa face starvation due to historic drought READ MORE :

Record number of trophy hunting firms selling sickening trips flock to UK show READ MORE :

Yet change is finally within reach. In just a few weeks, a new borehole funded by the Wimbledon Foundation and installed by WaterAid is due to transform life in Dina’s village, replacing dangerous daily journeys with clean water just minutes from her home.

‌



The change will also allow Dina to reclaim the career in carpentry she was forced to abandon when she had to move to the area to care for her ageing grandfather, who could no longer fetch water for himself. Since then, she has barely picked up her tools.

“My hope is that when my daughter grows up, she shouldn’t experience what I have wanted to become something people talk about as ‘once upon a time’, not something she has to live through,” she added.

I travelled to Malawi with chef and Great British Menu presenter Andi Oliver, 62, to see how something many of us take for granted - turning on a tap - can mean the difference between health and disease, dignity and hardship, and in some cases, life and death.

‌



View 9 Images They visit the toilet and shower facility at the center, part of the Wimbledon Foundation-funded projects (Image: WaterAid/ LeeAnn Olwage)

Andi said: “I just can’t imagine having to do that every single day and still be this positive, powerful, passionate and talented woman with such a clear vision for the future.

“As soon as I asked what she wanted to do when the water arrives, she just exploded with ideas. She’s got a business plan. Bringing water to this village is like turning a switch. It’s like turning the lights on, turning hope on, turning possibility on.”

‌



The consequences of unsafe water are visible everywhere. They affect children before school, families trying to grow food and women carrying the greatest burden of collecting water. But nowhere are the risks more stark than in maternity clinics.

View 9 Images Midwife Blessings Mwaleya in the delivery room (Image: WaterAid/ LeeAnn Olwage)

Sisters Eliza Brutula, 37, and Trinity Mbewe, 26, both gave birth at Kangolwa Centre in Chimbindu yet their experiences of becoming mothers could hardly have been more different.

‌



Hours after labour Eliza was forced to make a treacherous 10-minute descent to the nearby River Katete to wash herself using water contaminated by agriculture and other industries.

She said: “For me I accepted my fate. This is what I went through, but now when I see this generation... they’re able to go through it the easier way."

Eliza explained how some of her friends have had to make the journey during the wet season in muddy conditions adding: “if you fall into a ditch and you’re too weak to climb out, it could take a long time before anyone realises you haven’t come back. But after WaterAid installed a clean water supply at the clinic, Trinity simply turned on a tap after giving birth.”

‌



View 9 Images Dina Nyati washes dishes with her sister, Kelita Njati, at her home in Mkambisi (Image: WaterAid/ LeeAnn Olwage)

The difference is about far more than convenience. Without clean water, proper sanitation and hygiene, mothers and newborn babies are at far greater risk of life-threatening infections, including maternal sepsis.

Across sub-Saharan Africa, an estimated 36 mothers die from the infection every day, making women almost 150 times more likely to die than mothers in Europe and North America.

‌



Malawi bears one of the highest maternal sepsis burdens in the region, recording 77,536 cases in 2023 - resulting in 107 deaths. WaterAid says that clean water, toilets, and handwashing could cut maternal and newborn deaths in half.

View 9 Images The water system was installed in the Thundu community in 2021 (Image: WaterAid/ LeeAnn Olwage)

Loveless Chipokasa, 43, remembers giving birth before the clinic had running water. Desperate for a drink afterwards, she was told there was no water available. “They took a cup and stood by the roof to catch the rainwater,” she recalled.

‌



Margaret Zephena, 33, also gave birth before clean water reached the clinic and remembers making the same treacherous walk to the river after giving birth, only to be confronted by local people who complained that new mothers should not wash there. “I felt like my rights were being violated,” she said. “I’d just given birth. I wanted to wash. I wanted to feel good.”

View 9 Images Dina on her mega mission to collect water for her family (Image: WaterAid/ LeeAnn Olwage)

Today, both women have relatives give birth at the same clinic under very different circumstances, where turning on a tap has replaced desperate searches for rainwater and exhausting walks to the river.

‌



For many of us, access to running water is something we barely notice until it disappears. For Andi, that realisation came within hours of arriving in Malawi.

She said: “It definitely gives you perspective and makes me grateful for the life that I do have. But clean, accessible water is a human right. It’s not a favour. Everybody should be able to turn on the tap and get clean, accessible water.”

The effects of clean water do not end with better health- they can also shape an entire future. Just a few hours apart in rural Malawi, two 18-year-old girls are living remarkably different lives because of something as simple as whether they have a reliable source of clean water.

‌



Until 2022, Elshaday Gabriel spent up to an hour and a half every morning carrying 20-litre containers meaning she often arrived late for school after queuing. WaterAid installed three taps in her village Thundy four years ago.

View 9 Images A 10,000 litre capacity tank supplies the Kangolwa Health Center with clean water (Image: WaterAid/ LeeAnn Olwage)

“Now the water is nearby, I have more time to study,” she added. As a result, the teenager has secured a place at college to train as a nurse. Asked why she chose the profession, her answer is simple: “I want to serve my community.”

‌



For Lydia Konjwani who lives in the same village as Dina, that future still feels painfully out of reach. Every morning she wakes at 2am to begin collecting water before school, making repeated trips and queuing for hours before hurrying to class exhausted.

“I sleep at school because I’m tired,” she says. “If I didn’t have to wake up so early to fetch water, I would do better. I’d be able to concentrate.”

The consequences have already altered the course of her education. Last year she became so ill with diarrhoea caused by contaminated water, that she missed her exams and was forced to repeat a year at school. Her dream of becoming either a teacher or a police officer now feels uncertain.

‌



View 9 Images An estimated 36 mothers die from the infection every day (Image: WaterAid/ LeeAnn Olwage)

WaterAid is due to bring clean water to Lydia’s village in the coming weeks. Asked whether that could change her future, her answer comes without hesitation. “Yes,” she says. “Definitely.”

For 45 years, farmer Dyson Jambo relied on muddy river water that regularly spread disease but today he proudly grows tomatoes beside his home in Thundy using the village water supply. “My life is full of joy,” he says, explaining that having water nearby means he can irrigate his crops, monitor them every morning and sell the harvest for extra income.

‌



Nearby wash cooking pots under the tap, a simple task we take for granted but something that would have been impossible a few years ago.

Peter Phiri, WaterAid’s Malawi Country Director said:“Across Malawi, one in three people still lacks access to clean water. As a result, women face life-threatening risks during childbirth, newborns are exposed to preventable, often deadly, infections, and entire communities are held back, their potential limited by the absence of this basic resource.

“We’re proud of the progress in Ntchisi, where women can now give birth more safely and communities have the foundations to grow and thrive.”

Article continues below

Andi added: “People don’t want somebody else to transform their lives for them. Give them access to clean water and they can transform their own lives. That’s what people want.”

“Everything really does start with water.”

News.content:
London's spectacular Pride parade is underway with the streets a sea of colour as hundreds of thousands descend on the capital to line the streets.

Stages along the route will see some big names perform, including Grammy-nominated singer and producer, MNEK, who is headlining the main stage at Trafalgar Square, alongside artists, Beth Ditto and Meek. You can watch the parade here:

News.title: Berries will last days longer when kept in £4 B&M 'fridge basket'
News.content:
Berries will last days longer when kept in £4 B&M 'fridge basket'

The simple swap could help strawberries and raspberries last a few extra days

View 3 Images The container is on offer in stores across the UK for £4 (Image: © Keith Mayhew/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

B&M is selling a Berry Basket Container for £4 in stores across the UK. Aside from making your fridge look more aesthetic without mountains of supermarket plastic containers, the design is made to help fruit last as long as possible in the fridge.

‌



According to the product description, B&M said that shoppers can "keep berries/fruit together in one place". The container has two removable baskets to help "easily wash fruit" and store them.

‌



The B&M Berry Basket Container has a couple of design features that make it ideal for extending the shelf life of fruit, meaning less money and food gets wasted in your kitchen each week.

‌



The product's removable interior baskets act like mini-colanders. Keeping the berries slightly elevated off the solid bottom of the main outer box prevents them from sitting in their own condensation and trapped moisture, which is the number one cause of rapid mould growth.

Fruit fans can also pull the baskets out to wash their berries under the tap, let them dry, and put them right back in. By following all of the tips below, berries could last several days beyond what the supermarkets claim on the packaging.

View 3 Images The Berry Basket Container is on sale at B&M (Image: B&M)

‌



Even with a basket insert, if you put dripping wet berries into the container and seal it, the trapped humidity will cause them to rot. After washing them in the baskets, spread them out on a paper towel for up to 15 minutes to dry fully.

Go a step further and slip a small piece of folded kitchen roll into the very bottom of the main clear container (underneath the baskets). Any condensation that drips down will be absorbed by the towel instead of creating a humid pool at the bottom

Importantly, don't pack your fruit too tightly into the container. By giving the fruit a little room, air can circulate through the holes in the inner baskets and improve how long they are likely to last before going off.

‌



View 3 Images The £4 container has a clear lid and two separate sections for fruit (Image: B&M)

How else can I make berries last longer?

One of the biggest mistakes people make with strawberries, raspberries, and blackberries is washing everything at once. Introducing moisture is what leads to mould growth, so only wash what you plan to eat today.

Another error is keeping them in the plastic supermarket containers, which are best suited for shipping and display, not long-term storage in the fridge. Because the berries sit directly on the flat plastic bottom, condensation pools underneath them.

Article continues below

The berries at the bottom end up crushed under the weight of those above them, soaking up moisture, creating the perfect breeding ground for fuzzy mould. Berries will last longer if these 'bad ones' are quickly plucked from the container to prevent mould from spreading to the 'good' berries.

News.title: Hosepipe ban to start in days amid UK heatwave with Brits facing scorching 34C
News.content:
Hosepipe ban to start in days amid UK heatwave with Brits facing scorching 34C

Southern Water has issued a hosepipe pan from 12.01am on July 10 in Hampshire and on the Isle of Wight

View 2 Images A hosepipe ban with be in place in Hampshire and on the Isle of Wight (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

A hosepipe ban has been announced for part of the UK as temperatures are expected to peak at a sweltering 34C with another heatwave likely.

‌



Southern Water has issued a hosepipe pan from 12.01am on Friday, July 10, in Hampshire and on the Isle of Wight.

‌



The Met Office said temperatures are forecast to rise to 29C on Sunday, then approach the low 30s next week before a peak of 34C on Thursday or Friday in the South East.

‌



It is expected to be a prolonged spell of hot weather in parts of the UK, but it will not be as hot and humid as last month's heatwave, the forecaster added.

View 2 Images The UK is expected to be hit by a third heatwave (Image: AFP via Getty Images)
